title: Monarch Payments — MLOps handoff and integration notes
content:
Meeting: Monarch Payments — MLOps handoff call (follow-up)
Date: 2025-11-04 (notes taken 11/04, updated 11/06)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Diego Ramirez (Redwood), Aisha Patel (Solutions), Liam O'Connor (Monarch, Head of ML), Priya Nair (Monarch, Security)

High level summary:
- Monarch is moving their fraud-model serving off a fragile in-house cluster; wants Redwood Private (VPC) deployment for predictable latency and PCI compliance.
- Primary workload: real-time scoring for authorizations (per-request latency budget tight), plus batch re-scoring for audits.
- This doc captures requirements, gotchas surfaced during the call, proposed integration pattern, and concrete next actions for handoff to eng + infra.

Key requirements (explicit):
- P95 latency <= 45ms end-to-end for the online scoring path (from request hitting Monarch gateway to response returned).
- Sustained throughput: 1200 req/s, spike up to 6000 req/s for 30s bursts during peak settlement windows.
- Max model size: 8B parameters (currently using a distilled transformer variant).
- No raw PANs or full cardholder data may leave Monarch network — Redwood must operate inside customer VPC / private deployment.
- Audit logs retained for 2 years, redaction for PII in logs mandatory.
- Key storage: integrate with customer KMS + optional HSM for signing tokens.
- Canary rollouts for model updates (A/B 10%/90% initially) and ability to rollback automatically on error spike.

Constraints / non-functional notes from Monarch:
- Must pass internal PCI-DSS assessment — they will run us through their checklist (Priya).
- Network: Monarch runs in Azure region eu-west-2; we need to confirm supported region image and MTU/VPC peering constraints.
- Legal: contract needs data processing addendum and SOC2 addendum (already in procurement queue).

Integration proposal (high-level):
- Deploy Redwood Private in customer VNet as a dedicated stack (control plane isolated), with private API endpoints accessible only via internal ALB.
- Use mutual TLS + token auth for app->inference calls. Recommend short-lived tokens minted by Monarch auth service.
- Ingress pattern: Monarch will route authorization calls to a sidecar gateway that performs token exchange + basic validation, then call Redwood inference endpoint.
- For batch jobs, use SFTP drop or scheduled jobs invoking Redwood batch endpoints from Monarch batch network.

Performance tuning gotchas called out on call:
- Batching: default continuous batching may increase P95 if small-latency budget required. Need workload-aware batching config: low-latency pool (no batch) + throughput pool (large batch).
- KV cache: fraud model uses long session context for user history; ensure KV cache TTLs align with regulatory needs (avoid persistent PII caching).
- Tokenization differences: Monarch uses a proprietary tokeniser for certain fields — requires pre-processing step in customer infra or custom tokenizer assets uploaded to runtime.
- Embedding fallback: they plan to embed transactional metadata for similarity checks; watch costs on high-dim embeddings and consider down-projection or sparse indexing.

Security & compliance notes:
- Logs must be redacted before leaving VPC; propose a log filter lambda (customer-owned) that strips PAN-like patterns and PII.
- Key management: integrate with Monarch KMS (Azure Key Vault) + optional CloudHSM for signing. Need to validate Redwood Private connector for Vault access.
- Audit: Redwood must expose per-request audit id, model-version, and route metadata in logs for forensics.
- Pen-testing: Monarch requires an internal pentest window; schedule after we provision the environment and before go-live.

Data flow sketch (text):
1) Authorization request hits Monarch API GW -> sidecar token exchange -> forward to Redwood endpoint (private IP)
2) Redwood runtime does model inference (fast-path) -> returns score + metadata (model_version, kv_hit)
3) Sidecar attaches score, logs event id to Kafka topic (monarch-inference-events) with redaction, passes to downstream auth service
4) Batch re-score job runs nightly, results persisted to S3-compatible store (encrypted with customer keys)

Open questions (need answers from Monarch):
- Q1: Do they need synchronous response time measured from mobile app or from internal GW? (affects SLO placement)
- Q2: Clarify retention policy for intermediate KV caches — can we keep them encrypted for 7 days? Priya said "probably not"; need official policy doc.
- Q3: Exact tokenizer version and whether Monarch can provide the tokenizer binary.
- Q4: Will logs streamed to Monarch Kafka have consumer encryption in transit only or need at-rest encryption keys managed by Monarch?
- Q5: What is expected RTO for canary rollback? (They suggested immediate fallback if error > 0.5% for 10 min)

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Maya: draft high-level Redwood Private architecture diagram for Monarch (due 2025-11-07) -> include VPC peering, ALB, Vault connector, HSM options.
- Diego: validate runtime low-latency pool configs and rough cost estimate for dedicated capacity that meets 1200 req/s sustained + spikes (ETA 2025-11-09).
- Aisha: open ticket with Infra to confirm eu-west-2 base image availability and any region-specific kernel/hypervisor notes (Jira created: JIRA-MLINT-876).
- Monarch (Liam/Priya): share tokenizer binary and official data retention policy; Priya to share PCI checklist doc by 11/08.
- Maya + Monarch: schedule pentest window (target window 2025-11-20 to 11-22) after environment provision.

Risks and mitigation ideas:
- Risk: P95 target tough if sidecar adds variable latency. Mitigation: colocate sidecar in same subnet, pre-warm connections, consider direct private link.
- Risk: Log redaction failure causing exposure. Mitigation: dual-check pipeline: client-side redaction + server-side regex filter + sampling audit.
- Risk: Tokenizer mismatch causing inference drift. Mitigation: run integration test harness comparing token counts & model logits for small sample set prior to rollout.

Notes to self (quick):
- Build a short demo harness that mimics Monarch auth calls and measures E2E with sidecar in our staging.
- Add a prompt/serialization check in rollout pipeline to ensure input schema hasn't changed between model versions.

If Monarch pushes timeline: we should prioritize low-latency pool + canary controls first; secondary items (HSM, long retention) can be staged.

Action item follow-up cadence: weekly sync until infra provisioned, then twice-weekly during canary.

End of notes.
